rule: Release the issue's claim (restore the trigger label or move it to a visible blocked state) whenever a runner parks work without running it, and make the parked comment describe what actually re-triggers the work.
why: A parked issue stayed claimed with its trigger label removed and no sweep re-listed it, so it would never run even though the comment promised it would.

rule: Validate owner/repo and issue numbers parsed from issue bodies against a strict allowlist pattern, rejecting '.' and '..' segments, before interpolating them into any gh api path.
why: Unvalidated body-derived refs such as '../..#5' let an untrusted issue author redirect authenticated API calls to other endpoints or repositories.

rule: Memoize dependency-graph traversals per node with visited/visiting marking, and enforce depth, node, and concurrency caps that fail closed when exceeded.
why: Per-path recursion over author-linked issues reached roughly 10^11 paths, which would hang the gate while the issue stayed claimed.

rule: Apply the readiness gate on every path that can start work, including spec-advanced and carried-over issue ids, not only the primary listing.
why: A blocked issue was specced, parked, and then re-added from the spec-advanced carry-over and built anyway, because that path skipped the gate.

rule: Only let trusted root-issue data produce invalid, error, or failed results; content from other issue bodies must be ignored or treated as a leaf.
why: Any outside author who edits a dependency body could park trusted issues in needs-info or turn the scheduled sweep red with a non-zero exit.

rule: Track visited dependency nodes by identity and count distinct issues against the walk cap, so shared nodes are not refetched or double-counted.
why: Diamond-shaped dependency graphs were refetched and counted as extra visits, tripping the node cap and sending valid chains to needs-info.

rule: Do not edit files under .github/workflows or templates/github to wire new secrets or env; describe the exact edit (declare the secret in workflow_call.secrets, map it into the step env, update the callers) in the PR body for a human to appl…
why: The App credential shipped unreachable because the reusable workflows never declared or mapped its secrets, and the PR body omitted the hand edits that CLAUDE.md requires.

rule: When a preferred credential fails to mint, fall back to the next configured credential inside the resolver, and derive any logged credential label from the credential actually used.
why: A failed App mint silently dropped to the ambient GITHUB_TOKEN, so factory PRs got no CI while the logs still claimed the App token.

rule: Request only the GitHub App permissions the code actually uses, and keep the documented permission list identical to the permissions constant in code.
why: An unused issues:write scope made minting fail for Apps without Issues access and contradicted both the docs and the stated least-privilege intent.

rule: When a function gains a default that makes network or container calls, inject a stub for that dependency or disable its switch in the shared test options for every existing test that reaches that function.
why: Existing doctor tests reached the real npm registry because they did not stub the new default, so the suite became network-dependent and could time out on slow links.

rule: Throw on non-OK upstream responses instead of resolving to undefined, and never cache a failure result as if it were a successful lookup.
why: A single transient registry error resolved to undefined and was stored for the full cache TTL, so the hub kept reporting a lookup failure for an hour.

rule: Use `Refs #N` instead of `Closes #N` in the PR body whenever the PR does not deliver every item the linked issue or PR title names, such as a UI or action.
why: Using `Closes` would auto-close the issue even though the headline Update button and its UI were missing from the diff.

rule: Run `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and the affected tests locally before pushing, and delete any helper or variable the change no longer uses.
why: An unused test helper failed `pnpm lint`, which CI's `pnpm verify` runs, so the PR was blocked on a gate the author could have run locally.

rule: Substitute or remove every placeholder token (such as `YOUR_APP_SLUG`) in generated templates, and add a test that fails if any placeholder survives `apply`.
why: An unreplaced `YOUR_APP_SLUG[bot]` shipped as a live entry in every generated revise gate, and the existing test only checked the `YOUR_LOGIN` placeholder, so nothing caught it.

rule: Verify a test's or comment's premise against the base branch's current workflow files before asserting it, and state the real constraint (such as a lagging `@v1` tag) in the comment.
why: A new test asserted that no reusable workflow declared the App secret, but the base branch already declared and mapped it, so the test blocked the template change that would have made the feature work.

rule: Normalise CRLF to LF on both the pasted PR-body text and the manifest string before any substring comparison against human-edited content.
why: Browser-edited PR bodies use CRLF while manifest JSON uses LF, so multi-line items never match and a correctly pasted item stays missing forever.

rule: Escape or defang any manifest- or agent-supplied text before embedding it in a generated PR-body block, and locate block boundaries with markers that such text cannot reproduce.
why: Unescaped ids and descriptions let a reporter forge the human-paste boundary, so a block could be marked discharged with nothing pasted.

rule: Run PR-body state updates before any early return that skips the push, not only on the pushed-commit path.
why: Discharge ran only after a pushed commit, so a human who pasted the fix with no other code feedback never saw the disclosure update.

rule: When concatenating per-repository results into one combined list, sort the merged list by its timestamp (newest first) before returning it, and add a test that uses at least two repositories.
why: Each repository's results were appended in config order, so the newest run from a later repository was buried below older runs from an earlier one.

rule: Do not add a source file whose name differs from an existing file only by letter case, and check for case-only collisions before creating any new module.
why: A case-only duplicate (RepoFilter.tsx beside repoFilter.ts) resolves to different files on case-insensitive macOS and case-sensitive Linux, so it breaks on one platform while CI stays green.

rule: When one operation fans out across repositories, enforce a shared budget for expensive calls such as comment fetches and external CLI invocations across the whole fan-out, not a separate limit per repository.
why: A per-repository cap multiplied by the repository count produced roughly 16 concurrent gh processes on every refresh, exhausting the API quota the factory shares.

rule: When loading a persisted store, treat a present but invalid file as an error to surface, create defaults only when the file is absent, and never overwrite an existing file without a successful, non-clobbering backup.
why: A single malformed entry made the loader return undefined, so the next startup replaced teams.json with a bare default team and discarded hand-added teams and memberships without a log line.

rule: Keep read-only RPC handlers free of disk writes: compute derived state in memory at read time and persist only on explicit mutations.
why: list_teams and get_team rewrote teams.json whenever the project list had drifted, so on a read-only config volume they failed with EACCES even though the answer could be computed in memory.

rule: Keep pending sign-in state in a form that unauthenticated requests cannot evict: make the state stateless (an HMAC over nonce and expiry, bound to the browser cookie), or refuse new states at the cap instead of deleting unexpired ones.
why: Anonymous requests filled a bounded map and evicted in-flight states, so legitimate OAuth callbacks returned 400 and users were locked out of sign-in.

rule: Remove secrets from process.env once they are read, and register them for redaction before any child process is spawned.
why: The OAuth client secret stayed in the environment and was inherited by every spawned child process and its output, exposing it beyond the code that needed it.

rule: For every cookie-authenticated route, add negative tests for a foreign or missing Origin and for an invalid or expired session, not only the happy path.
why: Tests only sent the valid Origin, so a reorder of the auth and same-origin checks could silently allow cross-site requests carrying the session cookie.

rule: Redact persisted run output using the secret environment names registered at render or write time, not a snapshot taken before the run registers its provider keys.
why: A snapshot taken at run-accepted missed custom provider keys registered later in the run, so an opaque key echoed in a warning or run-error was written to the log in cleartext on the first run.

rule: Route every write failure in a persisted event log to the log's failure handler, which emits a warning and marks the log dead, instead of swallowing the rejection.
why: Swallowed append errors (ENOSPC, EIO, EACCES) left silent holes that the reader reported as a complete, untruncated history, contradicting the documented warning behaviour.

rule: Locate a run's persisted event log by an identifier written into the run record itself, not by the nearest timestamp at or before the record.
why: Nearest-timestamp matching returned another run's events for records that had no log of their own, such as CLI runs, failed log opens, or remote records.

rule: Before committing a base merge, treat any conflicted path that matches the CI-config (workflow) patterns as unresolvable and hold for a human, so the agent round never runs into the workflow guard.
why: A conflicted workflow file written into the worktree makes the sync-back throw an uncaught guard error, which spends the agent round and leaves the PR labelled as still revising with no comment.

rule: Reply to and resolve a review thread only when the round produced a diff that addresses that thread; a merge-only push must report zero addressed items and leave threads open.
why: Pushing a merge commit with no agent change while replying 'Addressed in commit' and resolving every thread misreports unaddressed feedback as fixed.

rule: Run the conflict-marker check immediately before the diff capture and push, after the repair loop, so repair passes cannot reintroduce markers unnoticed.
why: A repair pass that restores a conflicted file after the one-time marker check lets markers be pushed while the summary still reports the conflicts as resolved.

rule: When a change alters how a deployment mode or launch flow is selected, update every doc, compose example, and container config that describes the old flow in the same change, and mark the change as breaking.
why: Without it, existing container and reverse-proxy operators followed docs that no longer worked, and the hub stopped serving its web UI on upgrade with no escape hatch.

rule: Before delegating an unauthenticated route to a third-party auth handler, enforce a request body-size cap and set the handler's rate limiting explicitly rather than relying on library defaults.
why: Without it, anonymous clients could send oversized POSTs and flood the auth database with OAuth-state rows, because the defaults were unverified and rate limiting was off.

rule: Read secret environment variables once at startup, delete them from process.env, and add their names to the secret-scan list.
why: Without it, secrets stayed in process.env where every spawned child process inherited them and the outgoing-diff secret scan did not catch the leak.

rule: Name any persisted per-run artifact from an identifier the client already receives, and return that identifier in the run's events or listing so clients can address it.
why: The log was named from a timestamp no API exposed, so reads for every run except a task's newest returned silent empty pages.

rule: Do not await disk I/O on the path that releases a shared run slot; finish and dequeue the run first, or bound the write with a timeout.
why: A stalled volume write kept the slot marked active, so finishRun and startNext never ran and every queued run waited indefinitely.

rule: Re-assert state-path and symlink safety before every file write instead of caching the result from the first write.
why: Checking once and caching the path let a later symlink swap redirect appends outside the checkout, unlike the per-append check in appendMetric.

rule: Before force-pushing a rebased branch, require that every path differing between the rebased HEAD and the clean merge tree is among the files the agent was shown as conflicted, otherwise reset and hold.
why: Files that conflicted only at an intermediate replay stop were silently resolved to the branch's version, reverting base changes that would land on the base branch when the PR merged.

rule: When checking authorship or ownership across a branch's commit range, include merge commits instead of filtering them out with `--no-merges`.
why: A human merge commit carrying a hand conflict resolution passed the factory-ownership check, was then flattened by the rebase, and was force-pushed over.

rule: When a lease-protected or force push fails after the agent has run, post the failure as a PR comment and clear the in-progress label rather than letting the error fall into the generic catch.
why: A rejected push left the PR labelled as revising with no notice, so every round would run the agent and then fail silently.

rule: Validate any URL read from a run record or imported artifact by requiring a string type, parsing it with `new URL`, requiring the `https:` protocol, rejecting username or password, capping its length, and returning the normalized `href`.
why: Without these checks, non-string values passed through as links, userinfo hosts were labelled with a brand they never matched, and very long slash runs could block the hub's event loop.

rule: When `main` has changed files under `.github/workflows/`, rebase the branch onto `main` instead of merging it.
why: A merge left conflicts in workflow files that the push token could not resolve, so the branch stayed unmergeable until it was rebased.

rule: Add a test asserting the rendered href and label for every new user-visible link and every new server-side URL mapping before the change is considered complete.
why: Links shipped without tests for the run list, run detail, GitLab `web_url` mapping and Linear `url` mapping, so regressions in those paths would go unnoticed.

rule: Serialize every read-modify-write of a persisted credential or config file through a single promise chain, and give each temp file a unique name.
why: Overlapping set and delete calls read the same snapshot, so the last rename silently drops another entry after a success response, and a shared temp name makes renames fail with ENOENT.

rule: Before overwriting or deleting a secret value that the outgoing-secret scanner reads from process.env, register the displaced value with the redaction list.
why: Rotating a key while a run is in flight removes the old value from the exact-match scan, so that run can publish the old key unredacted.

rule: When storing an override for a provider credential, enumerate every environment variable the resolver checks for that provider in precedence order, and override or report all of them.
why: Writing only OPENAI_API_KEY leaves CODEX_API_KEY or CODEX_AUTH_JSON taking precedence, so Settings shows the key as set while runs keep using the old one.

rule: When a setting decides how CI or a runner behaves, store it in a tracked file or read it from the base ref, never from a git-ignored working-tree file.
why: A git-ignored config is absent in CI checkouts, so the CI run silently uses different defaults and refuses or retargets cards that the board showed as valid.

rule: Apply the same validation rules to a shared config value on every write path, including the Tauri command and the hub RPC.
why: When only one write path validated the branch name, an unsafe value saved through the other path later refused every unlabelled run.

rule: Reset form selection state (such as a target branch) when its project, options, or dialog session changes, so a hidden stale value is never submitted.
why: A previously chosen branch survived cancel, reopen, or project switch and was sent while the select displayed a different option, so the card targeted a branch the user could not see.

rule: Before wiring any self-update or installer path, confirm it cannot exit the app, overwrite a running sidecar, or leave child runs orphaned, and gate it on the hub reporting no active runs.
why: Without that check, installing an update can kill in-flight runs and replace files the running hub still uses, even though the UI told the user it would not.

rule: When adding a Rust dependency, run cargo build and commit the updated Cargo.lock in the same change.
why: Without a resolved lockfile the new code is never compiled in CI, and transitive crates float unpinned into a release job that holds signing secrets.

rule: Keep landing and README claims true on main, and link only to releases or features that already exist.
why: Without this, a Download button can point at a release that 404s until a maintainer publishes it, and the breakage ships with the next manual deploy.

rule: Trim and normalise input before running redaction or pattern matches on it, and assert the redaction holds for padded values, not only clean ones.
why: Anchored URL detectors missed a credential-bearing clone URL with leading whitespace, so the raw userinfo was written to the audit log while the clone still succeeded.

rule: Validate client-supplied and on-disk fields with the same type guard on both write and read before they are persisted or rendered, as sibling fields already are.
why: An unvalidated startedBy was persisted on the non-hub path and forwarded unchecked on read, so a non-string value could blank the Runs table and let any file writer forge attribution.

rule: When adding a state-changing hub RPC, either add it to the audit allowlist or state its exemption, and make the docs coverage claim match the actual list.
why: docs/hub.md claimed every state-changing action was audited, but spawn_run, kill_run and several draft writes were absent from AUDITED, so the documented guarantee overstated coverage.

rule: When filtering or routing published events by payload fields, derive the filter from the exact payload shape each publisher emits (including string and nested payloads), and add a test that subscribes as a restricted user and asserts that p…
why: The team filter matched only top-level repoPath/path objects, so no real event passed it and team members lost all live run and change updates while the filter had no test.

rule: When adding an authorization layer to an RPC dispatcher, enumerate every command in the catalogue and gate each one explicitly, including commands that look read-only, fleet-wide, or side-effecting on the host.
why: Commands such as browse_dirs, agent_cli_versions and api_cancel_complete were missed, so signed-in users outside any team could still reach host or cross-team functionality.

rule: When refusing access to a resource in a multi-tenant hub, return one identical, path-free message for unknown, unregistered and foreign resources.
why: Distinct refusal texts that echo paths let a member enumerate which repositories and run ids exist on the host and belong to other teams.

rule: When selecting which review's blocking findings to address, match the review marker to the PR's current head SHA and ignore markers from earlier heads.
why: Without this, revision rounds answer stale findings from older reviews, so the loop keeps cycling without clearing the findings on the code that is actually under review.

rule: When the base branch has changed CI configuration, rebase the branch onto the base and push with a lease-protected force push instead of merging the base in.
why: Merging the base failed because the push token may not write CI-config changes into the branch, which forced an extra rebase round.

rule: Keep a stated BLOCKING verdict whenever its file cannot be matched to the changed-file list, and treat a truncated diff as unknown rather than as an empty change set.
why: Unmatched file names and truncated diffs let the host downgrade valid blocking findings to a clean verdict, which bypasses the gate.

rule: Extract the review verdict and the re-review block only from the first non-blank line or a fixed position, never from text inside quotes or code fences.
why: Verdict text matched anywhere in the reply let quoted or fenced content override the reviewer's real verdict.

rule: When overriding Vitest `test.exclude` in a config, spread `configDefaults.exclude` (for example `[...configDefaults.exclude, 'e2e/**']`) instead of replacing the list.
why: Replacing the default exclude drops the nested `**/node_modules/**` pattern, so bundled dependency test files get collected and a local `pnpm test` can run them.

rule: Scope responsive layout changes to their breakpoint with `max-md:` (or equivalent) variants rather than applying flex-wrap or similar changes at every width.
why: An unconditional `flex-wrap` on the Needs-you header regressed the desktop layout, where long titles now drop to their own line instead of truncating.

rule: When adding a new test directory or Playwright spec, wire it into a CI or verify gate and typecheck it (add it to tsconfig or a lint step), and run the spec before claiming its assertions hold.
why: A new e2e spec that no gate runs or typechecks can fail on its first real step, leaving the claimed 390 px coverage unverified and free to rot.

rule: When a config field is superseded by a newer field, resolve it through a single shared resolver (new field, then validated legacy field) that every reader calls, including aggregators, settings UI, and board or task-creation code, rather th…
why: Readers that consulted only the new field showed existing projects under the wrong tracker, and separate copies of the fallback logic drifted apart.

rule: When a stored setting can be absent, give its select or picker an explicit empty option that represents the unset state, and never display a default value the config does not actually hold.
why: A select that showed GitHub for an unset config never fired a change event when the user re-selected it, so the value the board required was never saved and Save stayed disabled.

rule: Authorize team roles and visibility only on server-controlled, immutable identity (user id or provider-verified e-mail), and make authentication-library fields that feed authorization non-writable by the client, for example with `input: fal…
why: A signed-in user could post a forged `providerLogin` to `/api/auth/update-user` and gain admin rights over any team that listed that login.

rule: Pass the selected team or scope id to every server call that returns scoped data (projects, runs, tasks, needs-you items) and refetch when it changes, rather than fetching unscoped and filtering in the browser.
why: Without the id the server returns the user's first team's data, so switching teams shows the wrong or an empty list.

rule: Before writing code or docs that call hub RPC commands or describe access rules, confirm the command names, identity matching, and guards in the checked-out source, and do not rely on the issue title or on an assumed base.
why: The branch used command names and access rules that did not exist in the tree, so the UI called missing commands and the docs described behaviour the code did not implement.

rule: Never grant command or window permissions to wildcard remote origins such as http://*/* or https://*/*; scope each remote capability to a specific, validated origin.
why: A wildcard remote grant lets any page the window loads, including link targets and identity-provider redirects, call privileged commands and read or alter saved state.

rule: Reject glob or pattern metacharacters (*, (, ), {, }) and any host outside plain [a-z0-9.-] or a bracketed IPv6 literal before a user-supplied URL is turned into a capability URL pattern.
why: Unvalidated input such as https://* parses as a valid URL, so it silently becomes a wildcard grant persisted across launches.

rule: Enforce permission checks in the backend or capability configuration, never only in frontend UI conditionals such as hiding a button.
why: A UI-only check such as hiding Add for non-loopback pages is presentation only, so any page can still invoke the underlying command.

rule: Derive admin or authorization identity only from server-verified provider account data, never from user-writable profile or auth-update fields.
why: A member who rewrote a stored user-writable field before it was disabled could pass the admin check and change the instance credential and policy for everyone.

rule: When registering a structured secret for redaction, also register each parsed inner secret value (token fields, API keys) individually, not only the whole blob.
why: Redaction and the outgoing-diff gate matched only the full stored JSON, so inner tokens could leak into PR bodies, comments, logs, and delivered diffs.

rule: For a user-only credential run, strip every key environment variable the run's provider choice can read, and refuse the run when the user has no credential for that provider.
why: Stripping only a fixed list of names let custom providers and gateway base URLs fall through to the instance key while the run was recorded as user-credentialed.

rule: Before re-publishing a change that touches apps/desktop, run the desktop CI steps (`pnpm test:desktop` and `pnpm --dir apps/desktop build`) in addition to the root `pnpm run verify`.
why: Root verify does not cover apps/desktop, so a required prop missing from new tests passed the proof of work and then failed CI's desktop typecheck and tests.

rule: Derive a card's live state (running stage, repair count, receipt, PR link) from the live stage marker, and never from the last delivered run record.
why: Run records are written only at delivery, so a re-running card showed the previous run's receipt, PR link and repair note.

rule: When a UI needs only run summary facts, read them with the artifact-free reader (records and proof) rather than the reader that includes diffs and transcripts.
why: Opening a card downloaded every stage's diff and transcript over hub HTTP just to render a handful of facts.

rule: Before requesting review, merge the current base branch into the feature branch and run `pnpm test:desktop` and `pnpm --dir apps/desktop build`, not only the root verify.
why: The branch fell behind main twice, which produced textual conflicts in App.tsx and broke a CI-run desktop demo test and the desktop build that the root verify does not cover.

rule: Do not poll gh-backed hub endpoints on a fixed short interval in every tab; poll on demand, pause while `document.hidden`, use a long interval, or add a hub-side cache.
why: A 30-second interval running the uncached needs-you read in every open tab multiplies GitHub CLI and GraphQL calls on the shared quota.

rule: Build tab UIs with the shared `Tabs` components from `@/ui` instead of hand-rolling role=tablist and role=tab buttons.
why: Hand-rolled tabs lacked arrow-key navigation, tabpanel and aria-controls wiring, and diverged from how RunDetail already implements tabs.

rule: Do not derive Inspector load effect dependencies or refetch triggers from the current screen; use a screen-independent flag so moving between screens neither resets state nor refetches.
why: A screen-dependent allRepos flag re-ran the Inspector load effect on every Board/Runs and Settings/New Task move, overwriting the live-run focus and refetching all runs.

rule: Merge the latest main into the branch before changing navigation or screen names, and keep main's screen set rather than reintroducing removed screens or old filter APIs.
why: The branch conflicted with main after the navigation change landed, which forced a revision round to reconcile removed screens and replaced repository-filter names.

rule: Keep remote tracker calls off the synchronous list-response path, and cache their promises and failures so concurrent or repeated requests share one read.
why: Runs listing now awaits per-repository tracker reads with no in-flight dedupe and no failure caching, so opening Runs stalls on many calls and repeats failing calls on every refresh.

rule: Derive every task-id or run-record lookup key from the exact expression the producer uses (for example `spec-<slug>-<N>` and `revise-pr-<slug>-<PR>`), and build test records through the producer rather than hand-typed id literals.
why: Hand-typed test ids matched an id shape no runner emits, so real spec and revise records were silently dropped from the audit view and the review blocked the PR.

rule: Before treating a task's numeric suffix as a GitHub issue number, check the tracker prefix and query GitHub only for `gh-` ids.
why: Taking trailing digits from any taskId made a Linear or GitLab card display the history of an unrelated GitHub issue.

rule: Include a PR in an issue's history only when a run record or a closing reference links it to that issue, never on a textual mention alone.
why: Any same-repo PR that merely mentioned the issue had its merge and review verdicts merged into that issue's history, so outsiders could shape the audit record.

rule: Derive any value that gets persisted or later executed from server-side state, and reject a client-echoed value that differs from the server's derivation before writing.
why: Persisting the client-supplied repo slug let one hub user set the secret target shown to other users, which was a blocking security finding.

rule: Validate a record against the same rules before writing it, and derive hosts and URL patterns from configuration instead of hard-coding github.com.
why: Records that the reader later rejects were written anyway, so the dialog silently showed a "never started" state with no PR link and no error on self-hosted GitHub.

rule: Pass the store's config directory through the context object (ctx.configDir) to every hub store instead of reading process environment variables.
why: The checklist store read the process environment, so demo runs wrote into the user's real config directory and tests had to mutate process.env without restoring it.

rule: After editing apps/desktop/src/wire.ts or src/wire.ts, regenerate the mirrored copy and run the root wire drift guard (src/wire.test.ts) before handing off.
why: The desktop wire copy drifted from the generator output, so the PR's recorded verify run failed and the change could not be shown to pass.

rule: When changing files under apps/desktop, run that package's own typecheck and test suite (`tsc` and `vitest run` in apps/desktop) in addition to root `pnpm run verify`.
why: Root verify does not typecheck or test the desktop app, so the desktop changes had no recorded green run and CI could still fail after merge.

rule: When renaming a label or comment marker that shipped workflows create or listen for, keep accepting and writing the old spelling until every caller and template accepts the new one, and define that transition in the spec before implementing…
why: Preflight required the new names that no shipped workflow creates, and the review trigger label was renamed to one callers never listen for, so review and implement runs failed on repos that only had the old labels.

rule: Build label removals only from labels the item actually carries, and skip any removal for a label the repository may never have created.
why: A removal for a label the repo never created makes the whole GitHub edit fail, so hand-back and re-review steps silently break on unmigrated repos.

rule: Before pushing a revision, answer every blocking finding of the latest review as fixed, not fixed, or disputed in the revision summary, and do not change CI config to make a fix pass.
why: A revision was rejected with two blocking items unanswered, so nothing was pushed, and the fix had to work against the workflows as they already exist on main.

rule: Classify a revision round as a special case (merge-only, cap-exempt, re-review-skipped) only from what the round actually changed in git, never from keyword matches in feedback text.
why: A feedback item that merely mentioned the word "conflict" was treated as a merge-only round, so the agent never ran, real review items were marked addressed and resolved, and no re-review was requested.

rule: Scope a re-review's since-diff and changed-file set from the git range between the reviewed SHA and the head, never from a marker or list embedded in a bot summary.
why: Scoping from a summary marker hid edits to files outside the listed set from the reviewer and let the host downgrade their blocking findings, so unreviewed changes passed.

rule: Give every git fetch on a hub read or poll path a timeout and set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, reusing the existing FETCH_ENV and FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS helpers.
why: An unbounded, prompt-capable fetch behind the 5-second Home poll let one unreachable or credential-prompting remote hang the whole project list.

rule: Pass every link read from branch data, run records or other externally writable sources through httpsUrl() before it reaches an href.
why: A raw prUrl from the metrics branch rendered as an anchor skipped the link gate that local summaries use, so http, data and other non-https schemes could reach the UI.

rule: Have the run writer record a cost the provider did not report as unknown (omit costUsd or stamp costUnknown), never as 0, and have readers test that stamp rather than a numeric default.
why: Runs with no provider-reported cost were written as costUsd 0, so the hub showed a made-up $0.00 and counted those runs as priced, and the unknown-cost label could never fire.

rule: When reading a bounded page of MR or PR notes or reviews, fetch the newest entries first (sort=desc) or page through the full list, and reuse the existing newest-first helper rather than a single oldest-first page.
why: Reading only the oldest 100 notes misses late blocking reviews and the lesson marker, which produces a false clean-merge result and duplicate lesson notes on re-run.

rule: Check tracker label names through the shared label helper, accepting every known spelling, instead of comparing against one literal string.
why: A strict comparison against only the current label spelling made the verify-failed check false for legacy-labelled MRs and broke the test that asserted it.

rule: Before any model call, note post, or store write for an MR or PR, verify that it comes from the factory: same source and target project and a factory branch prefix.
why: Without that check, a fork MR author can supply text that reaches the lesson prompt and is injected into later runs' retrospective blocks.

rule: Treat a secret-scan hit in the pre-review gate as a hard stop: end the run as secret-blocked with the diff, transcript and finalText withheld, and never resume the implementer or give the agent the scanner's file or pattern details.
why: A repair loop lets a misbehaving or prompt-injected agent learn what the detector flags and ship a tree with the credential removed, leaving only a stderr line as trace and possibly leaking the secret-bearing transcript into run records.

rule: Test pipeline gating by calling the real orchestration function, and do not mock the stage runner with a copy of the gate ordering logic.
why: A mock that re-implements the gate sequence passes even when the real control flow is wrong, so the reviewer-skip path, the repaired diff handoff to the reviewer, and the post-review re-review went unasserted.

rule: Before any unattended merge, require the PR head's git tree to equal either the reviewed commit's tree or the tree of merging the base into the reviewed commit, and never rely on an equal `git patch-id --stable` alone.
why: `git patch-id --stable` ignores whitespace, so a whitespace-only push after review would keep the review valid and be merged unreviewed.

rule: Merge only when mergeStateStatus is CLEAN, and escalate instead of merging when any human review is CHANGES_REQUESTED or the PR carries the policy hold label.
why: Without these checks an act-mode bot merges PRs that a maintainer has blocked or that are BLOCKED, UNSTABLE, or UNKNOWN, landing unreviewed changes.

rule: Append the APPROVE decision record to the decisions log before calling merge, under its own dedupe key, and abort the merge if that write fails.
why: A shared per-head dedupe key let an earlier ESCALATE suppress the APPROVE record, so the log showed a merged head as ESCALATE and undercounted velocity.

rule: Do not read FETCH_HEAD after a git fetch that another concurrent operation can also run; serialize the fetch and rev-parse, or fetch into a named ref and read that ref.
why: Two parallel fetches overwrite the shared FETCH_HEAD, so a read can return the wrong tip and report existing data as missing.

rule: When a mutation reuses an existing PR or branch, update the PR title along with the body on every reuse.
why: A reused PR keeps its stale title after the content changes, so the title can misstate the mode or action the diff actually applies.

rule: Filter repository identifiers taken from shared metrics data to the project's own slug before passing them to gh or other privileged commands.
why: Any writer to the metrics branch could otherwise steer the hub's gh identity toward other repositories or fan out to thousands of gh processes.

rule: When code skips, deletes or repairs audit data it did not write, print a warning that names the affected file or path before the action.
why: Without the warnings, a recursive lock-directory delete and silently dropped bad lines went unreported, and the review treated that as a blocking finding that needed a second revision round.

rule: Before changing a shared parser's skip or keep behaviour, list every caller and check which ones write files back from its output.
why: Silently dropping non-object lines in the shared parseJsonlLines erased those lines the next time the metrics-branch code rewrote its files, and no test covered that path.

rule: When pruning rotated audit files, delete only a contiguous oldest-first prefix so the hash chain stays verifiable.
why: Exempting legacy files from the age prune removed files from the middle of the rotation set, and verify then reported a broken chain.

rule: When selecting the review that gates a merge, pick the latest eligible review first, then apply run-stamp and run-id checks to that selected review only; never drop unstamped or other-run reviews before choosing the latest.
why: Filtering by stamp before choosing the latest let an older clean review win over a newer BLOCKING review, which could merge a blocked PR.

rule: When adding a new hidden marker or stamp, add it to the marker-stripping pattern used for model-authored text and reject duplicate stamps the same way existing sole-marker checks do.
why: Without this, PR content can quote a run stamp to satisfy a run pin, and a planted second stamp is accepted.

rule: Make the pre-merge re-read re-check every input the original decision depended on, including the base tip against the decided base SHA, required check conclusions, and the decide() verdict.
why: A re-read that only checks PR state and policy can merge onto a base that moved or past failing checks while the docs claim nothing changed.

rule: Skip the `gh issue edit` or `gh pr edit` call when the computed add and remove flag lists are both empty, in every caller rather than only in the shared editor.
why: A flagless edit is rejected by `gh` when run non-interactively, so a retrigger that should be a no-op fails outright and the item is reported as failed.

rule: Compare and mutate label names only through the shared label helpers (`hasLabel`, `sameLabel`, `resolveAdds`, `resolveRemovals`), never with a raw `includes` or a direct `--add-label` or `--remove-label` flag.
why: A single-spelling check lets a legacy-spelled hold label bypass a merge gate, and a raw add on a legacy repo leaves both spellings on the item.

rule: Make test fakes reflect the label creates and lists that earlier steps in the same flow actually perform, and confirm the tested branch is reachable in production before asserting on it.
why: A fake that ignores a prior create lets a test pass on a state production never reaches, which hides dead logic such as an unneeded `resolveAdds` call.

rule: Give every bug-fix item in a PR its own test that fails on the base branch before marking the item done.
why: Without that test the #901 live-run fix had no guard, so the review blocked the PR as a missed acceptance criterion.

rule: When widening a data loader to all repositories for one screen, filter the result to the active project before passing it to per-project components such as Fleet.
why: Without that filter, Settings → Fleet counted other repositories' runs against this project's concurrency slots, a blocking regression.

rule: When tightening a CSP header, carry forward every source from the prior policy unless removing it is justified and documented.
why: Dropping the earlier ipc and http://ipc.localhost connect-src entries risked blocking Tauri IPC calls from the hub page.

rule: When a heading-based parser emits detail bullets as checklist items, keep the finding's heading in the output (as the item or as a prefix) so a label on a detail bullet never replaces the finding's title.
why: Emitting labelled detail bullets in place of their heading dropped finding titles and created extra checklist items the reviser had to answer.

rule: Compile regexes once outside loops, and strip fenced blocks in a single forward pass that tracks the open fence, instead of searching the remaining lines from each opener.
why: Searching ahead from every unclosed opener with a new RegExp per line made fence stripping quadratic, taking about 15 seconds on a 65 KB review body against 1 ms on base.

rule: Before approving a change to a heuristic parser, run the base and working-tree output side by side on every existing input shape, and add a test for each shape whose output changed.
why: Heuristic tweaks that were not checked against base input shapes introduced regressions that took four revise rounds to surface.

rule: Resolve a manifest item from a listed id using one canonical id form, and refuse to discharge when more than one item matches instead of taking the first hit across raw and encoded forms.
why: Matching `p.id === id || encodeId(p.id) === id` with `find` let a block for one item discharge against a different item whose raw id happened to equal the encoded form, or whose encoding collided.

rule: Build a passing run's proof-of-work tail so that both stdout and stderr keep their final lines, for example the last N lines of stderr followed by the last M lines of stdout, and never select a single stream.
why: Taking only stdout on a pass dropped stderr-reported summaries (such as Jest's), while taking the combined last 40 lines let noise from one stream push the pass summary out of the tail.

rule: In desktop tests, read the most recent call of a hoisted mock (use `.at(-1)` or `mockClear()` in `beforeEach`), and await every async state update that a test triggers before the test returns.
why: Indexing `mock.results[0]` on a mock that is never cleared checked the first test's call, and un-awaited `.then` state updates outside `act` produced flaky warnings that polluted the verify output.

rule: When a path-containment check builds its prefix as `root + separator`, handle filesystem roots that already end in a separator (`/`, `C:\`) and add a test that uses such a root.
why: With root `/` the prefix became `//`, so every real subdirectory was rejected and add, browse and clone all failed in the desktop app.

rule: After removing or changing dependencies in a Cargo workspace, regenerate Cargo.lock with cargo and never hand-edit it.
why: A hand-edited lock left orphaned package entries and missed dependencies, so a `--locked` build would fail and the lock would drift on the next build.

rule: Before editing, merge or rebase onto the current main and confirm that the diff's context and removed lines still match main, resolving conflicts by keeping main's existing guards.
why: A diff built on a stale base conflicted in four files and, if resolved by taking the PR side, silently dropped pre-merge guards and broke the typecheck.

rule: Make every pre-merge re-check fail closed: block when a fetch fails, when a SHA is empty, or when a comparison cannot be made, and never fall back to a cached copy.
why: Falling back to a stale local policy on fetch failure, or skipping the base-tip comparison when a SHA is empty, lets a kill switch or a moved base be missed and the PR merged anyway.

rule: Before implementing, turn every finding or acceptance item of the linked issue into a checklist and map each one to code and a test, and report any item left open.
why: Covering only about three of ten issue findings was flagged as a blocking missed acceptance criterion and forced an extra review round.

rule: When a git command runs in a temporary worktree or checkout that the tool creates, route it through the repo's hostGitArgs helper, which disables hooks and fsmonitor, so the target repo's hooks cannot abort the operation.
why: Without it, hooks that need installed dependencies fail in the bare temporary worktree and abort every mode change, including `off`.

rule: Do not convert a failed read of a metrics or ledger branch into an empty value that a later write can persist; surface the error instead.
why: A swallowed fetch failure reads as an empty branch, so the next append pushes a parentless commit over the real history.

rule: When changing values in a user-owned JSON config, edit only the target spans in the original text instead of parsing and re-serialising the whole file.
why: A JSON.parse and JSON.stringify round trip expands compact arrays, normalises numbers and rewrites unrelated lines, so a simple mode switch produces a reformat-only diff.

rule: Do not bake new-name defaults into container ENV or config; bake only the names users already set, so a user's old-name override still wins over the image default.
why: Baked TASKCELL_HUB_* defaults outranked users' VANGUARD_HUB_* overrides, which moved hub state to an unmounted directory and rebound the host to 0.0.0.0.

rule: When renaming a variable or identifier, grep the whole tree, including tests, typed globals and placeholders, and rename every reference in the same change.
why: Leaving window.__VANGUARD_HUB__ in AutoMerge.test.tsx after the global was renamed broke the desktop type-check on the merged tree.

rule: Do not add a new branch prefix to the factory-owned or trusted set until the factory mints it and every workflow gate matches it.
why: Recognising chore/taskcell-* before minting it let human branches with that name be treated as factory work by overlap holds, gc and approval checks.

rule: After changing a Rust dependency requirement in Cargo.toml, regenerate Cargo.lock with `cargo update -w` on the required toolchain, commit it, and confirm `cargo build --locked` and `cargo test --locked` pass before documenting any version …
why: Without a regenerated lock, the `--locked` gate fails and the documented minimum version (such as zip >= 9.0.5) is not actually pinned anywhere.

rule: When bumping a JS package specifier that must match another toolchain component, update package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml together in the same change so the lock records the new specifier.
why: CI installs with `--frozen-lockfile`, so a manifest and lockfile that disagree fail the install and block the PR.

rule: Make each test guarding a gate assert the specific value the change produces, and confirm the test fails when that change is reverted.
why: An assertion that holds with or without the change leaves the new gate logic untested, so a regression would pass the suite unnoticed.

rule: When a gate reads a policy file, treat a failed or missing policy load as a hold that blocks the action, never as an empty value that allows it.
why: When the policy could not be loaded, the hub card showed the hold as empty and could disagree with the runtime, which fails closed.

rule: List every change that needs a human, such as a CI config edit or an App token swap, under a required human-action heading in the PR body, and check the diff against that list before approving.
why: The PR omitted a required workflow edit, so the gated action could never run and the review had to block the merge.

rule: Keep read-only commands such as status checks on their existing source resolver, and apply any stricter git protocol policy only to new mutating paths.
why: Sharing a stricter protocol allow-list with `skills check` made pinned skills under operator `insteadOf` rewrites report `unknown`, so `--strict` stopped failing on outdated skills.

rule: When an atomic directory swap fails, restore the moved-aside backup in a catch block, and do not remove that backup in an unconditional finally block.
why: A rename that failed after the old skill was moved aside let the finally block delete the backup, removing the installed skill while the lock still pinned it.

rule: Before marking a requested finding as addressed in a revision, confirm that the diff since the prior commit changes the code that finding names.
why: A revision summary listed nothing as deferred while the requested installSkill fix was absent from the diff, so the requested fix went unverified.

rule: When a scheduled or background run is refused at admission (slot busy, queue full, per-project queue taken), leave the task in its pending state and retry on the next tick, and never mark it failed or discard the refusal reason.
why: Without this, a transient capacity refusal permanently fails tasks and freezes their dependents, while the board shows them as running.

rule: Every run started without a live user request must resolve the owning user's credential through the same policy as the interactive run API, refuse visibly when that policy denies it, and write the run-start and run-queue audit entries under…
why: Without this, scheduled runs fall back to host-level credentials, skip the credential policy, and appear in the audit log under a fabricated actor.

rule: Write state files through an exclusively created, uniquely named temp file, check every write path against the state directory and refuse symlinks, and never overwrite a stored file that failed to read or parse.
why: Without this, a repository-controlled symlink lets the hub overwrite files outside the checkout, and a corrupt store gets silently replaced with empty data.

rule: Do not rely on a label, comment or push made with github.token to start another workflow; start the downstream workflow explicitly with a token that can trigger it, or make the dependent step a manual dispatch.
why: A label applied with github.token fires no workflow, so the revise path never ran and the left-behind label hid the PR and blocked later retries.

rule: Route every GitHub call in the approver through the allow-listed gh wrapper, never through the raw runner, including read-only calls.
why: Reads sent through the raw runner skipped the allow-list, so the second guard layer no longer covered them.

rule: Apply the same gates to any new write path that acts on another PR as the merge path does: skip cross-repository heads, authors outside the factory list, and hard exclusions before pushing, commenting or labelling.
why: A dependents update selected PRs by branch name alone, so an outsider's fork PR could receive a merge commit, a comment and the trigger label.

rule: Before pushing or marking a rebase complete, search every changed file for conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `|||||||`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) and resolve each hit.
why: Committed conflict markers broke the desktop typecheck, build and tests and produced a blocking review finding.

rule: Resolve the skills directory once and pass that same value to the skill-listing endpoint and to every run path that validates skill ids.
why: Listing with one directory while runs validated against another let the picker offer skills that the run then rejected as unknown.

rule: Neutralise GitLab quick-action lines (such as /close or /label) outside code fences in any description text written back to GitLab.
why: Writing a stored description back verbatim could run quick actions as the hub's GitLab user.

rule: Check whether a CI variable or secret exists with a request that cannot return its value, such as a HEAD request or a key-only query, and never read a response body that could contain the value.
why: A GET on the variable endpoint returned the secret into the hub process, breaking the rule that the hub never reads secret values.

rule: Before writing any generated config file into a checked-out repository, lstat the target file and its parent directory and refuse to write if either is a symlink or not a regular file.
why: A committed symlink made the write land outside the repo or inside .git/hooks, where the next git command could execute it, and this happened before any push permission check.

rule: Mark a verification step as passed only when its specific expected job succeeded, and treat a finished pipeline that lacks that job as a failure rather than inheriting the pipeline's overall status.
why: Falling back to the whole pipeline's status let a missing doctor job count as passed, so the project showed as ready with nothing actually installed.

rule: Pass user-supplied or lock-supplied paths to git with `--literal-pathspecs` (or `:(literal)`) so a leading `:` or glob characters are not read as pathspec magic.
why: Without it, a path such as `:foo` lists a different directory with exit 0, which skips the symlink and file-count checks and lets a symlink be installed as a plain file.

rule: Throw `TaskcellError` rather than a plain `Error` from any code path a CLI command can reach, so the user gets a one-line message instead of a stack trace.
why: A plain `Error` from `publishForReview` passes through `skillsCommand`, which only formats `TaskcellError`, so the user sees a stack trace with the branch name buried in it.

rule: When changing a regex or parser that strips model-emitted blocks, keep the base behaviour for unclosed or truncated blocks (remove through the end of the reply, across lines), and add a multi-line truncated fixture to the tests.
why: Narrowing the unclosed-block match to the opening tag's line left the JSON of a truncated multi-line block in the posted comment, which the base invariant forbids.

rule: Treat a review reply as usable only when its first non-blank line is the verdict, and never hoist or scan later lines for a verdict.
why: Hoisting a verdict from a later line let an echoed 'Verdict: NO BLOCKING FINDINGS' become the posted verdict, which the approver can act on.

rule: When a shared review-outcome check changes, add a test in each runner that consumes it (PR and MR) for a completed reply without a verdict, rather than only updating fixtures.
why: Tightening a shared usability check changed GitLab behaviour while the MR path was covered only by edited fixtures, so the new outcome went untested.

rule: Select a CLI subcommand from the parsed positional command, never by scanning raw argv for a word, and only rewrite option shapes that already fail on the base parser.
why: Matching the token `stats` anywhere in argv changed how `--skills <dir>` parsed for run and watch whenever `stats` appeared as an option value, breaking inputs that worked before.

rule: When merging retry, repair or resume attempts into one run record, carry forward every derived per-run field (such as skill ids) as a union across attempts instead of letting the final attempt's values overwrite them.
why: Spreading the last attempt over the merged result dropped a skill used in an earlier attempt, so repaired runs were recorded as using no skills and skewed the comparison permanently in metrics.jsonl.

rule: When a transcript is withheld or cannot be parsed, omit the derived field from the record instead of writing an empty list, and make the aggregation treat a missing field as unknown.
why: Writing an empty list for withheld runs made them count as 'used no skills' in every skill's baseline group, which biased the stats.

rule: Derive any run outcome that changes how a run is classified or displayed from a typed signal the run itself persists, never from free-form agent or issue text.
why: Matching limit phrases in agent-authored final text mislabelled genuine failed stages as neutral provider-limit stops, hiding real failures from the Runs and task views.

rule: When a state change needs two label or field writes, create and add the new state before removing the old one, and report any write failure instead of swallowing it.
why: If the second write fails after the first removal, the issue ends with neither the hold nor the trigger, so the scheduled sweep never resumes it and the UI misreports the state.

rule: Bound per-item external calls made during list or board reads with a shared budget or a cache, and pass already-loaded items into detail views instead of re-reading the whole board.
why: Each board read fanned out into sequential gh calls per card and per repository, and Home and detail views repeated the full read, multiplying latency and API usage.

rule: Before adding nested connections or new fields to a shared API list query, compute its cost against the provider's per-query complexity limit, and keep the shared query at its base shape unless that cost is shown to fit.
why: Widening the shared Linear list query with nested relations would have been rejected on every poll, and mocked tests that answered any query hid the failure.

rule: When a dependency or blocker lookup fails for any reason, leave the dependent item unready for that poll rather than substituting an empty blocker list.
why: A failed probe set the blockers to empty, so issues with open blockers or future cycles were treated as ready and started.

rule: Classify a lookup result as a missing item only from a structured API error payload, never by matching free-text in transport or HTTP error messages.
why: A proxy 404 or 502 whose text contained "not found" was reported as a nonexistent issue, which posted a wrong comment and moved the issue to needs-info.

rule: Validate any value an agent wrote into a file against a strict host-side allow-list of characters and length before storing it or echoing it into host-stamped text.
why: An unconstrained model string read from an agent-writable rollout file could carry markdown, mentions or key-shaped secrets into public comments and job summaries.

rule: Take every pricing-table row from the provider's live model list fetched in the same run, recording the exact slug and fetch date, and never from memory or a rounded estimate.
why: Unverified or rounded prices, such as cache-read values of 0.13 versus 0.125, silently misstate estimated cost and fail the pricing check.

rule: When a total or row sums some priced and some unpriced entries, label it as partial in the same place the number is shown.
why: Presenting a partially priced sum as a complete figure misleads readers about the true cost.

rule: Before emitting a command or compose snippet that names a container image, confirm that the image's Dockerfile installs every binary the command invokes.
why: Without this check, a generated worker crash-loops at preflight on a missing binary, or fails only after paid agent work, even though the snippet was presented as working.

rule: Read a project's task source through the single shared resolver (resolveTaskSource) and never re-derive it from the git origin or a legacy field.
why: Re-deriving the source from origin sent projects configured for another source to a worker that polled the wrong place, and two resolvers disagreed on which field wins.

rule: Validate any repo slug or host taken from a local git remote with the existing anchored validators before interpolating it into a copy-paste shell command.
why: An unanchored host regex and an unvalidated slug let a crafted origin inject shell metacharacters into the generated command and misclassify the host.

rule: Tests that read or write process.env, CI variables, or home-directory credential files must inject a temp path and clear CI and GITHUB_ACTIONS, never touch the real environment.
why: Without isolation, a test wrote a false 'secret is now stale' note into the CI job summary and read the developer's real ~/.codex/auth.json.

rule: Do not describe a live run or external verification as completed in docs or PR text unless it was actually executed; record it as not yet run and keep the acceptance criterion open.
why: The smoke-test doc claimed a run that never happened, so merging with 'Closes' would auto-close the issue with its criterion unmet.

rule: Relay only fixed, mapped messages for upstream identity-provider errors to sandboxed processes and host logs, never raw error text from the response body.
why: Free-form IdP error text reached the untrusted cell and the public host log, contradicting the docs' statement that the sidecar never echoes IdP responses.

rule: Rebase the branch onto the current base and re-run the full verify command before requesting review, and never resolve a conflict by keeping only the PR side of a shared list.
why: Without it, a conflict on adjacent lines can silently drop another entry from a shared list, and the proof of work then covers a stale base.

rule: When you add a dedupe or identity option to a marker-comment helper, pass it through every call site that posts that marker, including shadow, kill-switch and fallback paths.
why: Without it, one mode keeps re-posting the same comment on every run while the docs claim the option covers it.

rule: Do not treat a bare username as proof of a bot or App identity; match on an identity the operator controls or on a viewer-authored flag from the API.
why: Without it, a user account that registers the same login can pre-post the predictable marker and suppress a human-facing comment or a revise round.

rule: When a precondition check gates a run, test it with only the one provider's own credential name set, with unrelated credential variables set alone, and with none set, not only the single happy path.
why: The gate admitted or refused runs based on unrelated variables, and a test that set only the matching name missed both directions.

rule: When a refusal marker guards a store, clear the marker before writing the store it guards, so a crash between the two steps never leaves a marker blocking a valid store.
why: A crash after writing the disk-key store but before clearing the marker left a readable store that every later load refused as undecryptable.

rule: Do not write a regex on untrusted text that has two adjacent unbounded quantifiers able to match the same characters (such as `[A-Za-z0-9]*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*`); anchor the leading part to an unambiguous class and add a timing test with a …
why: The ambiguous pattern backtracked quadratically, so one long issue description blocked the synchronous watch loop for seconds on every poll.

rule: Never evict per-issue dedupe or failure state by a fixed wall-clock age; evict only ids absent from the current listing, or derive the window from the configured poll interval.
why: With a user-set interval of 600 seconds or more, the fixed 10-minute window wiped state on every poll, so skip logs and comment reads repeated and failure counts never reached the error threshold.

rule: When assigning a new id from existing records, derive the next number only from records that pass the same validation used to read them back, and refuse creation if the generated id would itself fail that validation.
why: Counting ids from invalid entries with an unbounded digit pattern produced new tasks whose ids were later rejected as invalid, so they were silently dropped and the board stopped accepting tasks.

rule: Make security-relevant members of an identity or auth interface required rather than optional, so an implementation cannot skip the check by leaving them out.
why: With an optional member, an embedding identity can omit it, which silently skips the account re-check and trusts a stale snapshot.

rule: Pass any credential-bearing value, such as a source URL, through the audit scrubber before composing it into an audit target, and never rely on a composite target to be scrubbed.
why: A target built as repoPath:source starts with a slash, so the scheme-based scrub never runs and a pasted token is persisted in the audit log even when the request is refused.

rule: Create a fresh git skill source per request in long-lived hub handlers, and never share a module-level instance whose dispose() deletes state.
why: A shared singleton's dispose() in one request's finally deletes the trees that a concurrent request from another user or tab is still using.

rule: Treat a missing optional directory such as skills/ as an empty result instead of an error.
why: Throwing on ENOENT makes every project without a skills/ directory fail to load, so the intended empty state is unreachable.

rule: Compare GitHub label names case-insensitively (lowercase both sides) everywhere a trigger or marker label is matched, because the API returns the repository's own casing.
why: An exact-case comparison made a Retry that had really re-triggered the issue fail with a 'no longer paused' refusal when the repository's label casing differed from the configured trigger.

rule: Raise deliberate refusal errors outside any try/catch that rewraps messages, or rethrow them unchanged, so the user-facing text is not prefixed with a misleading status such as 'stays paused'.
why: A new refusal thrown inside a try block was caught and prefixed with 'stays paused', so the UI and audit log reported a self-contradictory message, and the substring-only test did not catch it.

rule: Check each new or edited regression test by removing the code it guards and confirming the test fails, and never delete an assertion that still holds after a behaviour change.
why: Tests stayed green with the best-effort write-failure catch removed and with the unmark ordering reverted, so those paths went unverified across two review rounds.

rule: Do not mark an acceptance criterion as met when the implementation contradicts its wording; amend the criterion on the issue, or change the design, before implementing.
why: Documenting a planted-marker lock-out as accepted while the criterion says it cannot happen forced a second blocking review and a revision that relied on a waiver never recorded on the issue.

rule: Wrap every filesystem failure from the credential store (rm, mkdir, writeFile on the marker) in CredentialStoreError with a path-free message.
why: A raw EISDIR from rm escaped the typed error and exposed the file path, so callers could not match the error type and the path-free message contract was broken.

rule: Recognise the approver's own comments only by an author signal a person cannot hold, such as viewerDidAuthor, and never by matching login names against App or bot names.
why: Login matching let a user account named like the App suppress the approver's act marker and shadow decision comment, which the review flagged as blocking.

rule: Do not write setup docs that reuse the factory App's own credentials when the approver must run under a separate identity; name distinct approver credentials in the example.
why: The example minted the approver token from the factory App's credentials, so following it made comments from the implement and revise jobs trusted for dedupe.

rule: Gate any write to a dependent on a pending-round check that covers the window from the needs-revision label being applied until the round starts, not only on the in-progress label.
why: Checking only the in-progress revising label let update-branch move the head under a queued revise round, so the round started against a changed branch.

rule: Set `default: false` on generated credential-carrying CI jobs so they do not inherit the project's top-level `default:` keys such as `tags`, which can route them to unintended runners.
why: Inheriting the project's `default:` tags sent the factory jobs to whatever runner those tags selected, which the issue had asked to isolate.

rule: Validate any generated CI stage name against the stages the project actually declares, and fall back to the manual-include path when no declared name is usable.
why: Falling back to a hard-coded `test` stage wrote a stage the project does not have, reproducing the 'chosen stage does not exist' failure with neither a valid stage nor the manual path.

rule: Make the server-side doctor confirmation fail closed: refuse to start the pipeline when the fresh CI file read fails or the file cannot be parsed.
why: Swallowing the fetch error and treating an unparseable file as having no unruled jobs let verify check a stale list and start the pipeline without the required confirmation.

rule: When a PR links an issue, implement every acceptance criterion of that issue with tests in the same PR, or retitle the PR and unlink the issue if only part of the work is included.
why: A PR that claims to resolve an issue but ships only a test-flake tweak fails review on every acceptance criterion and gets closed, so the real work must be redone.

rule: In test afterEach hooks, settle every open run and await its pending state writes before removing the temp config directory, instead of adding retries to rm.
why: A state write that lands after rm can recreate the directory, leak it in the temp dir, or surface as an unhandled rejection in a later test.

rule: When a UI effect is keyed on a state value that a user action may set again to the same reference, pass a fresh object (e.g. spread it) or a nonce so each action re-triggers the effect.
why: Re-clicking the same rail entry set an identical object reference, React bailed out, and the live run never opened on the repeat click.

rule: In dev and mock fixtures, express timestamps relative to now with a shared helper instead of hardcoded ISO dates.
why: Hardcoded dates rendered as relative time keep aging, so the demo shows values like '13Nd ago' that drift further every day.

rule: Write regression tests that invoke the changed handler or user action and assert the rendered result, and confirm they fail without the change.
why: Tests that read an intermediate data map or reuse an unchanged path passed with or without the fix, so the blocking bugs went unguarded.

rule: When rendering static pages through a dev server, force production mode and define `import.meta.env.DEV` as false so dev-only components and markup cannot reach the built output.
why: Without it, dev-only debug UI such as a viewport badge gets rendered into the public page and ships to visitors.

rule: Whenever you change, move, or add a user-visible string or default label in a localized section, update the locale mapping in the same change and add a check that fails when any English text in that section lacks a translation pair.
why: Without it, translations silently drop and the public localized page reverts to English, because the build only fails when a listed string is missing.

rule: Do not commit files that a build regenerates; keep generated output directories gitignored and out of the commit.
why: Without it, each build rewrites tracked artifacts, which creates noisy diffs and may embed machine-specific paths such as /workspace.

rule: When a feature promises a behaviour for every view an acceptance criterion names, implement and test it for all of those views (including the aggregate or all-items view) rather than narrowing the scope in code or docs.
why: Polling was first added only for the single hub board, which left the tracker boards and the all-repositories view unrefreshed and failed the stated criterion, costing a full revision round.

rule: In background refresh loops, keep the last good data on screen when a poll fails, including per-item failures reported inside a successful response, and retry on the next tick instead of resetting to a loading state or dropping the item.
why: Routing a failed background poll through the full reload path unmounted the open board and quick view, discarding typed drafts and replies, and a repository failure reported in a successful response still dropped its cards.

rule: Derive the provider name and cause in every refusal or error message from the check that actually failed, and never state a reason the code path did not hit.
why: Messages that blamed the wrong provider or gave a false cause (such as 'no sidecar fronts it') steered users to drop the proxy, which would expose the credential in the sandbox.

rule: Add a test that asserts a security-sensitive credential is routed to the proxy and absent from sandbox secrets for each proxy-mode flag value, so reverting the wiring fails the suite.
why: The proxy-mode wiring could be reverted while the full suite stayed green, so a real key could reach the sandbox unnoticed.

rule: Before any hub code path starts an unattended agent run from a label or event, check the issue author with the same trust rule the watcher uses (isTrustedIssueAuthor) and fail closed when the lookup errors.
why: Without that check an outsider's labelled issue starts a run on the hub host with the hub's instance credential, bypassing the documented 'only listed accounts start the factory' gate.

rule: Keep 'never set' distinct from an explicit value in persisted settings, and never write a default value for a field on a write that does not change that field.
why: Writing enabled:false from a Run doctor click silently stopped hub-board scheduling, although the docs say only an explicit off should stop it.

rule: Build a command for another CLI parser by running that parser and checking the result kind; never cast an object to a command type to satisfy the typechecker.
why: A cast hid that a bare doctor call parsed to an error, so the doctor ran with no repo path, source or provider and reported on the wrong target.

rule: In tests whose behaviour depends on CI detection, stub the CI environment variables (for example GITHUB_ACTIONS and GITLAB_CI) to empty so the assertion does not depend on the environment the suite runs in.
why: Without the stubs the test passes on a developer machine but fails when the suite runs inside GitHub Actions, so the PR's own CI goes red.

rule: When a time-window bound makes a read path skip older records, keep a small capped fallback scan past the window so that states which depend on the last-seen timestamp, such as stale, remain reachable.
why: Dropping every record outside the window silently removed the stale state and the date of the last run, a regression that only a read-path test through the real reader would catch.

rule: When relaxing a fail-closed check on markdown or quick-action content, do not strip code blocks with a line regex; either keep the whole-body refusal or parse with the same markdown parser the downstream consumer uses, and refuse when any p…
why: A regex that treated any column-0 triple-backtick line as a fence let a /close line nested in a tilde fence, HTML block or comment through, so a quick action ran under the hub identity.

rule: For every security refusal gate, add test cases the new code must refuse that cover the parser's edge cases (nested or longer fences, indented or whitespace-trailed closers, alternate fence styles, HTML blocks), not only the forms the chang…
why: The new tests covered only fence forms the regex already rejected, so the bypass shipped without any failing test.

rule: When inserting user-supplied text into a string, pass a function replacer to `String.prototype.replace` or `replaceAll` instead of a replacement string, so `$` sequences are not interpreted.
why: Tags containing `$$`, `$&`, `` $` `` or `$'` were silently rewritten, or spliced the template into the generated YAML, producing a different tag or an invalid file.

rule: When deriving optional pre-fill data as part of a shared plan, catch failures locally and return an empty value with a note, so the plan, apply, verify and start steps still succeed.
why: An un-copyable optional setting made plan, apply, verify and start all fail for projects that never used that setting, which was a regression from the base behaviour.

rule: Write the PR title or squash commit subject as the user-visible behaviour change, not as the bug it fixes, because release-please copies that subject into the release notes.
why: A title that only restates the defect leaves the release notes silent about a tightened refusal that operators need to act on.

rule: When a guard forbids deleting or adopting a file, apply it on every path that can reach that file, including the first-save path where no secret exists yet.
why: A guard that covers only the deferred re-key branch still lets a planted credentials.key be adopted when no secret exists.

rule: Wrap new filesystem calls in the store's typed error without including the path, and never swallow a caught error without logging its code.
why: A raw fs error leaks the full path, and an empty catch leaves the operator unable to tell EISDIR, EACCES or EROFS apart.

rule: Before committing a generated output file, run `git ls-files` on its path; if it is already tracked, remove it from the index with `git rm --cached` so the existing ignore rule takes effect.
why: Adding or keeping a .gitignore entry does nothing for files that are already tracked, so generated outputs stayed committed and the PR's no-build-artifacts goal was not met.

rule: When a data table mirrors values defined in the app source, derive it from that source at build time or add a check that fails on mismatch, instead of hard-coding a copy.
why: Hard-coded copies drift silently from the app, leaving stale comments and fixture values (such as a state name no fixture carries) that no existing check catches.

rule: Apply reserved-name and collision checks to the runtime stage name after reference resolution, not to the name declared in the config.
why: A stage declared with a harmless name can resolve to a reserved name such as after-implementer, so the record overwrite the check was meant to prevent still happens.

rule: When a fix changes an existing success or refusal rule, leave the original regression test's fixture unchanged and add a new test for the new case instead of editing the old fixture until it passes.
why: Editing the old fixture hid a regression where a scheduled re-trigger was refused as no longer paused although the base code returned success.

rule: When a filter list is empty, treat it as meaning every repository in scope, and derive hints and unset-repo sets from all of those repositories rather than from only the open project.
why: Limiting an empty filter to the open project silently dropped repositories without a task source from the board, leaving no explanation and a blank board when there were no tasks.

rule: When a change alters the error class a function throws, assert the class (for example with toBeInstanceOf or toSatisfy) and not only a message substring.
