why: Substring assertions such as rejects.toThrow('preflight failed') still pass for a plain Error, so a change from a plain Error to a CliUsageError went unguarded by tests.

rule: Treat a poll as a shared outage only when no listed issue could be read, and still post each issue's own failure comment when other issues in the same poll succeed.
why: Suppressing comments whenever two or more issues fail hid persistent, issue-specific lookup failures indefinitely (0 comments after 40 polls versus 2 on the baseline).

rule: Match hold-comment markers exactly as written, punctuation included, rather than normalising away characters such as the trailing colon.
why: Normalising the marker let a human comment that merely starts with similar words count as the bot's hold comment, which caused spurious re-posts after a restart or a `watch --once` run.

rule: Never loosen or delete an existing assertion bound to make a test pass; when a bound looks wrong, fix the expectation and its comment together and assert exact counts.
why: A deleted upper bound and a comment that contradicted the code let a log-frequency test pass even when the every-10-polls behaviour was broken.

rule: When a gate holds a merge or push, return a status the caller turns into a visible outcome (a hold comment or a status change), never a neutral skipped status that leaves the PR silently unchanged.
why: A clean merge-only round returned skipped for a base CI change, so no comment was posted, the PR stayed in needs revision, and the branch was never updated.

rule: Pass --no-renames to every git diff --name-only that feeds a CI-path or deletion gate.
why: Rename detection printed only the destination path, so a workflow moved out of a CI directory escaped the gate and the resulting merge commit deleted it.

rule: When an option or env value is wired into a mocked call, assert the arguments the mock receives (for example with toHaveBeenLastCalledWith and objectContaining) so that reverting the wiring line makes a test fail.
why: Without that assertion, the reviewed PR's one-line wiring change could be reverted while every test still passed, leaving the key behaviour untested.

rule: In tests for code that reads an env, build the env with the same helper production uses, not a hand-written object, so inherited variables such as host auth paths are present as they would be in real runs.
why: A hand-built env that sets CODEX_AUTH_FILE to a missing file hid the real case where the host file is inherited and could be written, so the test passed while the production path was unverified.

rule: Before redirecting a credential update away from a shared store such as process.env, check every run type that later reads that store, and keep updating the shared store for those types.
why: Moving the rotated token into a per-run copy for all hub runs stopped instance-credential runs from seeing rotated tokens, so the next run was refused with a dead refresh token.

rule: When removing a transport or mock branch, search the whole desktop tree, including test files, for imports and calls from the removed library (such as `@tauri-apps/api/mocks`, `clearMocks`, `mockIPC`) and delete them in the same change.
why: A test file still imported and called `clearMocks()` from the removed Tauri mocks, so the PR was blocked and needed a manual fix.

rule: When removing a feature gate, confirm that every build that previously passed the gate (including the dev and mock builds that agents and e2e tests drive) still shows the feature, and state any intended visibility change in the PR.
why: Removing the hub gate silently hid the Fleet screen in the browser dev build, which agents and Playwright use, and nothing in the PR said this was intended.

rule: Before writing recovery copy for a failed connection, confirm that the suggested action (such as reloading the page) actually clears the stored token or state that caused the failure; if it does not, name the action that does.
why: The restart banner told browser users to reload, but the reload re-read the rejected token from sessionStorage, so the banner came back.

rule: Use a closing keyword for an issue only when every acceptance criterion is either fixed or has its own linked follow-up issue; otherwise reference the issue without closing it.
why: Merging auto-closed #1113 while five of its eight items were neither fixed nor split out, so those items lost their only tracker.

rule: For every new persisted field, add a test that reads it back from the written record and a test that older records without it fall back to the default.
why: The new maxRepairIterations field had no on-disk test and the legacy fallback in repairCap was untested, so the reviewer flagged both gaps.

rule: When a validation rule must hold on both sides of a process boundary, such as host and sidecar, define it once in a module both sides import, and never keep a duplicate in step with a comment.
why: A duplicated control-character regex, justified by a wrong 'cannot import' comment, forced a blocking revision, and the host and sidecar token checks drifted so a token the sidecar saved could be refused by the host.

rule: When a cleanup or teardown routine can be triggered by several signals or callers, keep a single in-flight teardown promise and return it to every concurrent caller instead of taking fresh snapshots on each call.
why: A second signal arriving during teardown took a new proxy snapshot while the first call was still removing sandboxes, which reopened the ordering race that sandbox-first teardown was meant to close.

rule: Do not cache a failed upstream lookup (an undefined result or a rejected promise) for the full TTL; evict it so retries and manual refresh can succeed.
why: A transient ls-remote failure was cached for 60 seconds and the Refresh button could not clear it, so the update button stayed hidden.

rule: Write a concurrency-cap test with more distinct inputs than the cap, and assert that the observed peak actually reaches the cap.
why: The test used only two sources, so a peak-at-most-four assertion passed even with no cap at all.

rule: When restricting an RPC to the hub owner, gate the matching UI actions on the same role and state the permission change and its rationale in the PR body.
why: Non-owners kept seeing Add, Remove and Update buttons that always fail, and the owner-only change had no recorded rationale for reviewers to confirm.

rule: When a dependency lookup fails, park the issue with a marker the resume sweep can retry once, and have the sweep skip only the marker that records a repeated failure right after a resume.
why: Skipping every failed-lookup park stopped automatic recovery from transient outages, so issues stayed under the waiting label until a human re-labelled them.

rule: Keep volatile error text such as HTTP status codes or timeout messages out of the comment body that is deduplicated, or dedupe on a stable marker instead.
why: The reason text changed on every poll during an outage, so the dedupe never matched and GitLab posted a new note on each poll.

rule: Route every source's comment dedupe through the shared postUnlessRepeated helper instead of a per-source comparison.
why: Linear kept its own comparison and bypassed the shared dedupe that the acceptance criteria required, so the change had to be reworked.

rule: When a load hook's read fails, clear the data it returns, and keep previous data only while a re-run is in flight, never after an error.
why: Keeping the last successful stats after a failed read showed another repo's numbers in ConflictStats, which was flagged as a blocking regression.

rule: Before marking a PR that cites an issue with several bullets, fix each bullet or link a follow-up issue for each deferred one with the reason it waits.
why: Citing the issue as 'Part of' without per-bullet status left the acceptance criteria unmet across two review rounds.

rule: Import shared file-layout names such as prefixes, suffixes and paths from one module in every reader and writer, and describe a layout as having a single source only once every reader and writer uses it.
why: The audit module's comment said the layout was written in one place while the run-events and run-store writers still hard-coded it, so readers and writers could drift apart.

rule: Declare a CommandPolicy for every new hub command and register it in HUB_POLICY in src/hub/commands/index.ts, because defineCommands and the command completeness test both require it.
why: Without the policy, typecheck and commands.test.ts fail, and at runtime dispatch throws on an undefined policy, so every capability read falls back to allowed.

rule: Gate each UI control on the same owner, write and remote flags as the hub command it invokes, not on a generic mutationsAllowed check.
why: A team member saw an enabled 'Open update PR' button for an owner-only command, and the hub then refused it with a 403.

rule: Rebase onto current main and rerun typecheck and the command completeness tests before trusting the PR's proof of work.
why: The branch's base lacked the HUB_POLICY block, so tests passed on the stale tree but failed on the current one.

rule: When reading a store whose id counter field is missing or invalid, derive the counter from the highest well-formed id in the file, and never let a removed id be handed out again.
why: Stores written before the counter existed read as lastId 0, so deleting the newest task and creating a new one reused its id, letting two tasks share one id in the archive, run records and audit targets.

rule: When a full store snapshot replaces the file, tag it with a new generation id and have the journal writer stamp every line with that generation, so the reader skips journal lines from any other generation.
why: If the journal is removed only after the rename, a crash in between replays stale edit lines over the new store and can bring back deleted tasks or undo the last edit.

rule: After any async gap before a scheduled task starts, re-read the task under the store lock and confirm it still exists and is still in the expected state before admitting the run.
why: A task deleted or archived while the scheduler was checking credentials and run limits still started, which could open a pull request for a task that no longer exists.

rule: When an issue asks for one shared abstraction, build it and route every reader of that data through it, rather than changing a single call site and leaving the other readers on hand-threaded inputs.
why: The first attempt changed one call site and left other key readers on hand-threaded env and key lists, so the review blocked it for not meeting the issue's main acceptance criterion.

rule: When redaction switches its secret source from process.env to a run-specific env, mask the union of both so host secrets remain redacted.
why: Reading only the run env dropped the host's provider keys from base-red redaction on hub user runs, a redaction gap that the review treated as a regression.

rule: When a change moves a computation into one shared step, switch every caller in the same change, including revise and no-change paths, to read that step's result, and grep for the old primitives to confirm no second computation remains.
why: Leaving revise-pr recomputing gate-config after the refactor drew a blocking review and forced a second revision round.

rule: When centralizing a computation, remove any result or callback field that no remaining consumer reads, so the typed result is the single source of truth.
why: An unused raw diff left in the result and callback input invited future callers to recompute from it, which is the duplication the change was meant to remove.

rule: Close each CodeQL alert in code, or dismiss it in code scanning with a reason a reviewer can check; a code comment alone never closes an alert.
why: Without this, the alert stays open on main after merge, and the PR needed two revision rounds to address the same blocking finding.

rule: When replacing an lstat symlink refusal with an O_NOFOLLOW open flag, keep the lstat-based refusal too, because constants.O_NOFOLLOW is undefined on Windows.
why: Without it, a symlinked hub store or journal is read and parsed on Windows, where the base branch refused it.

rule: Confirm that each regression or performance test fails on the pre-fix code before merging, using a bound that the old code actually violates.
why: Without this, the timing test passed on the old regex (about 306-329 ms against a 500 ms limit), so it guards nothing.

rule: Split any comma-separated provider list before validating it, and apply the split in every consumer (preflight, doctor, auth, workflow passthrough), not only in the parser.
why: Passing a raw `codex,cursor` string to single-provider resolvers made `watch` fail preflight and blocked the factory from using a fallback list.

rule: When a stage hits a provider limit, cool down only the entry that stage actually used, identified by its own pick, and never by matching provider names against the fallback agent.
why: Cooling the implementer's or fallback's entry when a reviewer or other stage hit the limit, or cooling a healthy entry that shares a provider name, writes false limits and breaks weighted rotation.

rule: Add at least one test that triggers a provider limit inside the real runner loop and asserts the recorded cool-down and the next entry chosen, instead of testing routing with an injected predicate.
why: Tests that stubbed the cooling predicate passed while the actual *** path was broken.

rule: When matching numbered bold finding titles, require whitespace or the closing `**` after the punctuation, so bold lead-ins that merely start with a number (such as `**1.5x slower**` or `**10:30 deploy**`) are not treated as findings.
why: Without that boundary, a bold lead-in that starts with a number is counted as a finding and hides the real bullets beneath it, so the checklist silently drops real items.

rule: When fixing a parser bug reported from a real review, add the regression test using that exact review text as a fixture and assert the expected item count, rather than a synthetic example.
why: A made-up layout can pass while the real reported layout, with its own headings, verdict lines and bullet styles, still fails, so the original bug is not shown to be fixed.

rule: When rebasing a branch that rebuilds a per-command option table, re-check every flag that workflows, templates and spawned argv pass against the new declarations before merging.
why: A flag that main added after the branch was cut (`--pinned-only`) was missing from the rebuilt table, so the CI invocation fell through to help and exited 0 without doing its work.

rule: Assert that every CLI invocation used by workflows and templates parses to a non-help result, not merely that it avoids a refusal error.
why: The invocation test only failed on error messages, so an undeclared flag that returned help passed silently and hid the missing `--pinned-only` declaration.

rule: When calling a hub command that requires a repoPath, pass the same repo source the detail pane uses (e.g. `liveRun.repoPath ?? project`), and never fall back to an empty string.
why: In single-project mode the active-run rows lack repoPath, so the empty-string fallback made the hub reject every read and the row silently stayed on Cell, which was the bug the PR was meant to fix.

rule: In tests that mock a hub or IPC call, assert the arguments it receives or make the mock reject invalid arguments the way the real endpoint does.
why: The mock resolved for any arguments, so a blank repoPath that the real hub rejects passed the test and let the bug through.

rule: When adding an RPC that attaches a credential to an outbound request, add an audit entry for it or check the caller's owner flag in the handler.
why: The PR was blocked because the credential-sending RPC was registered as a plain read with no audit record and no owner check, so any team member could trigger it unlogged.

rule: Apply the origin allowlist to every outbound request sent to a repo-chosen URL, whether or not a credential is attached.
why: Gating only keyed requests left keyless fetches to arbitrary repo-configured hosts open, which keeps a blind SSRF and host-probe path alive.

rule: Do not rewrite another module's user-facing error text with string replacement; export a boolean or origin-level helper and write the message locally.
why: Find-and-replace on another module's message silently stops matching when that wording changes and can show misleading text for endpoints from a different config source.

rule: When a copy or sync step filters out a security-relevant entry, record it in the returned report and assert on that report field in the test, not just on the absence of the file.
why: Filtered entries that were neither logged nor reported left a likely attack attempt invisible, and the original test only checked that the file was absent.

rule: When an integrity check runs after a write into a worktree, restore the original entry before throwing, and skip any host git commands in that worktree.
why: A replaced `.git` pointer left on disk let the subsequent cleanup `git status` run through an attacker-controlled config, which is the code-execution path the change was meant to close.

rule: When you change a function's input contract, update every caller, including contract and smoke tests, and every doc comment that describes that input, in the same change.
why: The interface comment and the contract smoke test kept describing and calling the old input, so they no longer tested what production runs.

rule: Before removing a permission from a remote or hub grant, confirm against the linked issue's acceptance criteria and the UIs already deployed from older releases that the removal does not break their close or navigation path, and raise any c…
why: Removing core:window:allow-destroy from remote origins broke older hub UIs that close the window through that permission, which forced several rounds of native close fallbacks before the criterion was dropped.

rule: Do not add a timer-based native window destroy that can override a page-side discard prompt or pending-write flush; let the page own the close decision and keep the prompt and flush path intact.
why: A native fallback fired after a fixed delay closed the window even after the user chose to stay at the discard prompt, which loses unsaved edits.

rule: Give each Tauri capability grant a unique identifier per origin (for example including the port), and surface a failed grant to the user instead of only logging it with eprintln.
why: Reusing a fixed identifier such as "local-hub" on every hub restart left stale per-port grants or, if the repeat was rejected, silently removed the local UI's server-switcher permissions.

rule: When a change adds a new workspace or package, wire its typecheck and tests into the root verify command or CI, or write the exact CI edit into the PR body for a human to apply.
why: The mobile app's typecheck and tests never ran in CI or the root verify, so a broken build could merge unnoticed.

rule: Attach a catch to every async UI event handler and show the user an error message, rather than discarding the promise with `void`.
why: A rejected disconnect was dropped silently, leaving the UI showing connected with no feedback while the token stayed in the keychain.

rule: Merge request headers with `new Headers(init?.headers)` instead of object-spreading them, because spreading a Headers instance or tuple array yields an empty object.
why: Spreading a non-plain headers value silently drops the auth token, so the request fails with a misleading 'bad hub token' error.

rule: Reset a reconnect backoff only after a stream frame has actually been received, never on connection open alone.
why: Resetting on open let an endpoint that returns 200 and closes immediately reconnect and reload the list about once a second with no backoff growth.

rule: Check the subscription's abort signal after every await and before invoking any handler, so a closed subscription cannot fire callbacks.
why: A superseded subscription could otherwise consume the new stream's one-time catch-up reload, set a rejected flag, or start a reconnect timer that tears down the live stream.

rule: Install a workspace's dependencies and run its own typecheck and test scripts before claiming they pass, and report exactly which ones ran.
why: The mobile typecheck and Jest suite never ran because apps/mobile had no node_modules, so its new tests were unverified while the PR still reported passing checks.

rule: Gate sensitive actions on `LocalAuthentication.getEnrolledLevelAsync()` (fall back to the dialog only when the level is `SecurityLevel.NONE`), not on `isEnrolledAsync()`, which ignores device passcodes.
why: A passcode-only iPhone skipped the passcode prompt and got a plain tap-through confirmation for a remote merge, which is weaker than the spec required.

rule: Guard every async action that can be triggered by a tap with a `useRef` in-flight flag, not only a `busy` state flag, so a second tap before re-render cannot submit again.
why: A `busy` React state flag only disables the button after re-render, so two fast taps can send the same reply or merge twice.

rule: Restore every `jest.spyOn` in an `afterEach(() => jest.restoreAllMocks())` hook rather than at the end of the test body.
why: A spy on `Alert.alert` that is never restored, or restored only after assertions, leaks into later tests and can make them pass for the wrong reason.

rule: Do not import from apps/desktop/src in apps/mobile; put helpers that mobile needs in packages/hub-client/src, which Metro watches, and have desktop re-export them.
why: Metro only watches packages/hub-client, so a mobile import from apps/desktop/src fails the bundle with a SHA-1 error and takes every tab down, while Jest and tsc still pass.

rule: Before merging a change to mobile imports or Metro-dependent code, run `npx expo export --platform ios` and `pnpm test` in apps/mobile, and do not rely on root `pnpm verify` alone.
why: Jest and tsc can pass on code that Metro cannot bundle, and root verify chains steps with `&&`, so a failure in an earlier step skipped verify:mobile and its new tests never ran.

rule: When helpers move into packages/hub-client/src, move their tests there too instead of leaving them under apps/desktop.
why: The root vitest run and lint only cover packages/*/src, so if the desktop re-export is removed, the helper tests silently stop running.

rule: For mobile live event streams, reuse the existing reconnecting watch helper (watchHub) instead of opening a bespoke /events subscription, and make it react only to change signals, not to every frame.
why: A custom subscription with no retry left the view stuck on 'Status: running' after a hub restart or network drop, and reading the event log on every frame from any repo caused a steady stream of full-file reads on the hub.

rule: When showing the tail of a hub run log on mobile, fetch only the recent window instead of paging from id 0 through the whole file, and filter stream events to the active run before triggering any read.
why: Paging a long log from the start costs one full-file server parse per page, which is quadratic for a 50-line view, and an active run can end up following an older run's log and wrongly show 'ended'.

rule: Gate a retry or action on the exact id format the backend validates, copying its regex, instead of a loose negative check such as 'not gh-N'.
why: A loose check showed Re-run on GitLab, Linear and long-form ids that the hub always refuses, so the button failed on every tap.

rule: When the issue lists several surfaces for one action, wire the action on every listed surface and add a test for each one before handing off.
why: Leaving out the Home item surface meant the spec's required Re-run was missing there, and the review blocked the PR over it.

rule: After a state-changing action succeeds, disable its button until the data refreshes so a second tap cannot resend the request.
why: Without this, a second tap sent a duplicate request that the hub refused, and the finding stayed open across revisions.

rule: Never deliver a session credential through a custom URL scheme redirect; use a flow that requires the user to confirm sign-in inside the app, such as a device authorization flow.
why: Any installed app can register the same scheme and receive the token, and PKCE alone did not stop a link that started the flow with the attacker's own challenge, so the revision was rejected and the PR closed.

rule: When mounting Better Auth plugins on the hub, disable any client-facing endpoints and header-exposing hooks the server does not call itself, such as `oneTimeToken({ disableClientRequest: true })` and `bearer()` response headers.
why: Leaving the plugin's generate endpoint and the bearer [REDACTED] header public lets browser scripts turn the HttpOnly session cookie into a readable token, which removes the cookie's protection against XSS.

rule: Build any URL the hub returns to a client, such as a verification or sign-in link, from the configured public base URL, and never from the request's protocol or host.
why: Deriving the scheme from an internal request URL produced http:// links behind an HTTPS proxy, so the first hop went over cleartext and sign-in broke or could be intercepted.

rule: When the client abandons a sign-in or fails after receiving a session token, revoke that server-side session on every abort and error path before discarding the token.
why: Dropping the token locally on cancel or a failed follow-up request left a valid session on the hub for its full lifetime, with nothing able to revoke it.

rule: Open a server-supplied verification URL in the app only after checking that it is http(s) and has the same origin as the hub URL the app connected to.
why: Passing the hub's returned URL straight to Linking.openURL let a cleartext man-in-the-middle or hostile hub make the app open other schemes or phishing pages.

rule: Send every stored push registration through the existing caller recheck before notifying, and never trust a stored owner flag as proof of current ownership.
why: Owner-flagged registrations bypassed the recheck, so phones kept receiving repository item titles after a local-to-server mode switch or an owner id change.

rule: Record newly seen items as notified on every pass, including passes with zero registered tokens, so a later (re)registration only records and does not push a backlog.
why: Returning early when no tokens exist skipped recording, so reconnecting after a full disconnect pushed every item that appeared in the meantime, contrary to the documented first-pass behaviour.

rule: In setup docs, make every command recipe self-sufficient: include the flag that writes the client credential, the step that shows the user where to read it, and the server-mode and public-URL settings needed for the client to complete sign-…
why: Without this, a user who copies a recipe gets a hub that prints no usable token in server mode, so the phone cannot connect.

rule: Do not document a command that exposes a hub on a public hostname unless it also sets the server-mode flag and the public origin, including quick or test variants.
why: A local-mode hub on a public URL keeps owner powers and has no sign-in gate, so the token becomes the only protection.

rule: In hub route tests, assert the exact expected HTTP status (for example toBe(200)) instead of negated checks such as not.toBe(403).
why: Negated status checks still pass on 400, 401, or 500 responses, so regressions in the accepted path go undetected.

rule: When a periodic job can start a new pass while the previous one is still running, chain the passes or skip the tick, and make close() await the actual in-flight work before tearing down the resources it uses.
why: Overwriting the pending promise made close() resolve early, so a late pass could still write files or call identity lookups after they were deleted or closed.

rule: When an issue's acceptance criterion says no other copy of a pattern remains, grep the whole repository for that pattern, including scheduler and RPC call sites, before marking the criterion met.
why: The PR claimed the duplicated visibility check was fully consolidated while the scheduler and RPC paths still carried their own copies, which blocked the review.

rule: Give every outbound network call on a shutdown path an explicit timeout or AbortSignal so that teardown cannot wait on a stalled remote endpoint.
why: An unbounded fetch to a push endpoint could hold up hub close for minutes and keep the instance lock held, where shutdown previously returned immediately.

rule: Classify provider errors only from the provider's own error text (its structured error payload or stderr), never from a combined message that embeds stdout or agent-written output.
why: Generic status and 'unauthorized' patterns matched ordinary agent output, so unrelated failures were reported as refused credentials and operators were told to rotate secrets that still worked.

rule: Check usage and rate-limit classifiers before auth classifiers, and make each classifier exclude matches from the others.
why: A session-limit failure whose output contained a 401 line was headlined as a refused credential, hiding the real limit message.

rule: When adding a user-visible notice or a persisted run-record flag, add a test that asserts it in the rendered output or the written record, not only the in-memory outcome.
why: Without those tests the PR notice and run-record flag went unverified, and a blocking review had to request them.

rule: Take a card's pull-request address for waiting-item matching from every run source, including CI-imported runs, while keeping CI runs out of card placement and view.run.
why: Cards whose only runs came from CI lost their 'Pull request ready' item and their Home waiting count because the PR address was read only from local runs.

rule: Read GitHub needs-you items whenever the repository has a GitHub remote, regardless of the card's task source, matching the behaviour of list_needs_you.
why: Linear, GitLab and hub-board cards lost their GitHub pull-request waiting items because the GitHub read was gated on the task source.

rule: Serve board polls from the shared needs-you cache, with a TTL at least as long as the poll interval, and skip per-item comment fetches on board reads.
why: A 15 s cache under a 20 s board poll missed on every poll, so each board read issued several gh lists, a login lookup and up to 30 comment fetches.

rule: When changing how a hidden comment marker is trust-checked, matched or stripped, list every tightened or loosened case in the PR body and add a test for each one.
why: Silently tightening the lesson-comment trust filter for a dedicated bot account made every rerun repost the lesson, and loosening other reads went unmentioned, which blocked the PR.

rule: When counting occurrences of a marker, match its full opener including the colon and payload grammar, never the bare marker name.
why: Counting the bare name `taskcell-pr-review-run` made a prose mention of the stamp count as a second marker, so the approver stamp check returned undefined and rejected a valid review.

rule: Make the marker dedupe helper throw when given a marker text that matches no declared kind, rather than returning false.
why: An undeclared marker returned false from the dedupe check, so the comment was reposted on every run with no error, and nothing flagged the future caller.

rule: Do not weaken gate config such as tsconfig lib, lint or coverage settings to make a type or lint error pass; fix the code that triggers it, or get the issue to explicitly ask for the change.
why: Lowering the desktop tsconfig lib from ES2023 to ES2022 to silence a type error was blocking, and it was only reverted after a revise round.

rule: Keep parse-only modules (parse.ts, args.ts, parsers.ts) free of imports of command runners, so that any non-CLI caller of parseCli does not load the whole CLI.
why: Routing parsing through the registry dragged every runner into the hub's type and load graph, which broke the desktop type check and slowed startup.

rule: Type command dispatch tables as full Records over every command kind with no casts, and fail at compile time when a kind has no runner instead of falling through to a silent exit.
why: A Partial table plus an early return on one kind let a new command kind with no runner compile and exit 0 without doing anything.

rule: When migrating callers off a wrapper layer, delete every wrapper whose only job is to forward its arguments to the same command, and point its callers at the client call directly.
why: Leaving about 74 pass-through wrappers in place failed the acceptance criterion and blocked the PR until the migration was finished.

rule: When a client filters server events through a hard-coded name list, add a test that checks the list against the server's published event names, or subscribe to whatever names callers request.
why: Events added on the server that are missing from the list are dropped silently, with no error and no failing test.

rule: Clear the connection-issue flag on the next successful stream frame or catch-up, and stop retrying permanent HTTP failures such as 401, 403 and 502 instead of retrying them forever.
why: Without this, the Lost connection banner stays on after the stream recovers, and a permanent failure is retried every 30 seconds indefinitely, adding noise to the hub logs.

rule: When a dedup check or SHA lookup fails, keep the base behaviour of still processing the item, and record the failure separately so the exit status reflects it; never turn a transient lookup error into a skip.
why: Treating a failed user or notes lookup as 'already reviewed' filtered out every labelled MR, so reviews stopped entirely where the base branch still reviewed them.

rule: Classify a usage-cap stop as paused only after the park step (onFailure) has succeeded; if parking throws, report the item as failed so --once exits non-zero.
why: When the label edit that parks the item threw, the item was still reported as a clean pause, so --once exited 0 while the item stayed stuck on the reviewing label.

rule: Recognise the factory's own bot comments only by `user.type == 'Bot'` with login `<slug>[bot]` (REST) or by `viewerDidAuthor === true`, and never by a bare login such as `<slug>`.
why: A bare login can be registered by a human account, so trusting it lets anyone inject lesson text into later agent runs, while `gh pr view` reports the App's comments under the bare slug, so the dedupe check never matched real comments.

rule: Keep App-identity checks used for dedupe out of the shared `trusted` filter, so App-authored comments never feed lesson notes, blocking-review counts or revise-round counts.
why: Adding the App identity to the single trusted predicate let the App's own comments reach the lesson model and the review counters, which widened trust beyond the dedupe scope the issue asked for.

rule: When aborting a spawned git or other subprocess that may start network helpers, spawn it detached with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, kill its whole process group on abort, and reject without awaiting the child, instead of relying on cancelSignal, …
why: Surviving transport helpers held the inherited stderr pipe, so the execa promise never settled and the tip lock was never released.

rule: When a cached value is served again, keep the timestamp of the original upstream read rather than stamping the time it was served, so staleness limits measure the real age of the data.
why: Re-stamping on every cache hit let last-good items outlive the 10-minute limit by up to the cache TTL, because the age was counted from the last served call instead of the last GitHub read.

rule: When testing timeout or abort behaviour for a subprocess, use a real hung child process (for example a local listener that never responds) and assert that the call settles and the lock is released, rather than a fake reader that only checks…
why: The original test only asserted signal.aborted on a fake reader, so it passed while the real timed-out fetch still held the tip lock.

rule: For each UI behaviour change, add a test that asserts the resulting visible state after the action (for example, the button is enabled again and the list is closed), not only that a callback was called.
why: Without that assertion, removing a state reset leaves every test green while the button stays disabled and the list stays open.

rule: Before reading a run's local event log, check the run's source and skip the read unless it is local, because imported CI runs have no local log.
why: Without that check, imported runs silently lose their detail, and a local run with the same task id and timestamp can supply the wrong data.

rule: When copy must differ by mode, remove the non-matching variant from the served HTML at the edge or build step rather than hiding it with a CSS display rule.
why: CSS-only hiding left live-hosting claims in the served markup, where crawlers, text browsers and agents still read them next to the "not open" copy.

rule: Test edge rewrite logic by running the real rewriter or worker against the built pages, not a hand-written stand-in for it.
why: A regex imitation of HTMLRewriter passed its checks without exercising the production selector and removal path, so a mismatch could only surface after deploy.

rule: When moving or rewriting tests, port every assertion from the old test to its replacement and confirm the new test still fails if the behaviour it guards breaks.
why: Dropped assertions (verdict placement, taskId, the negative 429 case, the no-resume call count) left regressions that no test would catch.

rule: Test ordering and wiring by calling the real production entry point and asserting on the arguments that reach each collaborator, never through a test-local helper that reimplements the sequence.
why: A helper that already runs the steps in the right order passes even when production reorders them or passes the wrong value, so the test proves nothing about the code.

rule: Before requesting review, make every acceptance item from the issue either fixed in the diff or closed with a one-line reason written in the PR body, since reviewers check the body and not the revision chat.
why: Items that were fixed or deliberately skipped but had no reason in the PR body kept the review blocking across two rounds.

rule: In any catch that falls back to a default, such as treating a failed lookup as not-found, log the error through failureReason(err) from src/core/errors.ts instead of silently returning a value.
why: A silent fallback in the lesson dedupe check would hide an expired token or a parse failure, and a re-run could then post duplicate lesson comments with no trace in the logs.

rule: When changing a path-redaction regex, keep every prefix form the previous pattern redacted, including `../` and `./`, and add a test row for each form.
why: Adding `.` to the lookbehind let `../../srv/...` and `./home/...` server paths reach Slack notes unredacted, which was a security regression.

rule: In a React effect that loads data keyed by taskId or repo, reset the stored value at the top of the effect before the new read starts.
why: Without the reset, a failed read for the next run kept the previous run's flow on screen instead of showing 'unavailable'.

rule: Answer every blocking review item as fixed, not fixed, or disputed in the PR before requesting another revision round.
why: Four unanswered blocking items made the automated revision fail and forced a manual fix.

rule: When a process signal hook re-raises the signal or branches on listener counts, register it with prependOnceListener and decide the re-raise from the listener count taken at registration, because Node removes once-listeners before invoking …
why: A listenerCount==0 check inside the hook misreads the app's own shutdown handler as gone, so the process dies before graceful cleanup such as hub.close() can finish.

rule: For each new side-effecting behaviour, add a test that asserts the observable effect (for example the exact process.kill call and its arguments, or a cleared timer) and confirm it fails when the implementation is reverted, rather than only …
why: Tests that only check registration pass even when the hook body does nothing or a cleanup timer is reverted, so the regression ships unnoticed.
